To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a modern pollen data set from Siberian tundra and taigas is established and applied to a lake sediment core from the Arctic Siberian lowlands.
a modern pollen-climatic relationship from the arctic forest transition zone was established.
a new modern pollen data set from the Siberian tundra and taigavegetation transition zone is presented, which fills the gap of previous regional pollen-climate transfer functions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the establishment of modern pollen–climate relationships and their application to a Holocene climate reconstruction in the Arctic.
the development of a new modern pollen-climate calibration set from the arctic forest limit in northern Siberia and its application to a Holocene climate reconstruction.
the development of a modern pollen–climate transfer function for a tundra–taigatransition zone in Siberia and its application to a Holocene lake record.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
climate conditions were warmer and wetter during the early to mid-Holocene and colder and drier during the late Holocene than today.

the Holocene climate history of the Siberian Arctic was characterized by moderate climate variability, with the exception of the early Holocene, and that the climate was not significantly warmer than present during the early to mid-Holocene, in contrast to previous assumptions.
the Siberian Arctic is not yet a region of pronounced temperature increase and that the Arctic amplification effect is not yet fully developed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Siberian Arctic was warmer and moister during the early and mid Holocene, but the climate conditions during the last 400 years were similar to those today.
we provide a pollen-climate calibration set for the tundra and the taiga in Siberia and apply this data set for a Holocene climate reconstruction from a Siberian lake.
the Siberian Arctic tundra and taigas provide a valuable data set to study past and future environmental changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

pollen-climate transfer functions are applicable to reconstruct Holocene climate in the Arctic Siberian lowlands, which is important in light of current climate change and the associated ecological consequences.
pollen data sets are needed from the tundra–taige transition zone to better understand past and future climate changes.
the pollen data set from the Siberian lowlands provides a useful tool for the reconstruction of past vegetation dynamics and climate in this region.
